newsitem.title: USA: US FCC proposes plan on phone line extensions.
newsitem.headline: US FCC proposes plan on phone line extensions.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission proposed Monday to allow phone companies -- without FCC approval -- to expand into new geographic areas they are otherwise eligible to serve.

Under the proposal, which implements last year's telecommunications law, carriers no longer would need approval before building, buying, operating or transmitting services over an extension of any line of communication.
Under existing law, carriers must get FCC certificaiton that the extension was consistent with the public convenience and necessity.
The new FCC plan distinguishes between "extensions" and "new" lines and tentatively concludes that "new" lines will continue to require FCC approval.
